title: Finite amplitude of unbounded quasi-coherent global sections
statement: Work in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and $X$ an algebraic space over $S$ with its small etale structure sheaf $\mathcal O_X$ [def-trf-algebraic-space]. Use module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], their unbounded derived category $D(\mathcal O_X)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], and its full subcategory $D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_X)$ of objects with quasi-coherent cohomology [def-trf-space-quasi-coherent-module]. Assume $X$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated: every open cover of $|X|$ admits a finite subcover and the absolute diagonal is quasi-compact. Let $R\Gamma(X,-):D(\mathcal O_X)\to D(\operatorname{Ab})$ be derived module global sections computed using K-injective resolutions [def-pur-ringed-site-zeroth-hypercohomology]. There exists an integer $N\geq0$, depending only on $X$, such that for every $E\in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_X)$ and every integer $t$ the following hold: if $\mathcal H^i(E)=0$ for $i>t$, then $H^mR\Gamma(X,E)=0$ for $m>t+N$; if $\mathcal H^i(E)=0$ for $i<t$, then $H^mR\Gamma(X,E)=0$ for $m<t$. The first implication allows $E$ to be unbounded below, and the second allows $E$ to be unbounded above. No bound on the Krull dimension of $X$ and no Noetherian hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Tag 08F7, lemma-application-nice-K-injective, part (3), applied to module global sections; the existence of a finite cohomological bound on quasi-coherent sheaves is spaces-cohomology.tex Tag 072C, lemma-vanishing-quasi-separated. Lower bound also follows from derived.tex Tag 05TC, lemma-negative-vanishing. This is the global-sections amplitude used in the proof of Tag 09MB.

proof.text: Put $F=\Gamma(X,-)=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal O_X}(\mathcal O_X,-)$ as in [def-pur-ringed-site-zeroth-hypercohomology]. This is additive. Kernels of module sheaves are sectionwise by [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], so a section family of a kernel is precisely a section family sent to zero. Thus $F$ preserves kernels and is left exact [def-sp-left-exact-additive]. The product universal property gives $F(\prod_nM_n)=\prod_nF(M_n)$: a map from $\mathcal O_X$ to a product is exactly a family of maps to its factors. This argument does not require $X$ to be an object of its small etale site.

source.place: Tag 08F7, lemma-application-nice-K-injective, hypotheses (1)-(2); elementary verification for global sections

proof.text: Choose $C\geq1$ from [lem-sfb-space-qcoh-cohomology-finite-bound]. The module category is Grothendieck by [prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist]; $\operatorname{Ab}$ is the category of $\mathbf Z$-modules and is Grothendieck by [lem-weil-pbc-ring-modules-grothendieck-abelian]. For a quasi-coherent $M$ and $p\geq C$, [lem-sfb-ringed-site-global-module-abelian-cohomology] gives $H^p(R\Gamma(X,M[0]))\cong H^p(X_{\mathrm{et}},M_{ab})=0$. By [lem-sp-kinjective-computes](2), the left side is $R^pF(M)$ computed by injective module resolutions. Thus the finite-bound hypothesis of 08F7 holds for this $F$ and this one $C$, uniformly in $M$.

source.place: Tag 072C, lemma-vanishing-quasi-separated; module/abelian global comparison is sites-cohomology.tex Tag 03FD; bounded-below injectives are K-injective by derived.tex Tag 070J

proof.text: Set $N=C-1\geq0$. If $\mathcal H^i(E)=0$ for $i>t$, apply [lem-sfb-space-product-preserving-derived-functor-upper-bound] with its $N$ equal to $C$, its $b=t$, and $F=\Gamma(X,-)$. Steps 1-2 verify left exactness, countable-product preservation and $R^pF(M)=0$ for $p\geq C$ on all quasi-coherent modules. Its derived functor is our $R\Gamma$, since both are computed on K-injective resolutions. It yields $H^mR\Gamma(X,E)=0$ for $m\geq t+C$, equivalently for $m>t+N$. Its statement imposes no lower bound on $E$.

If $\mathcal H^i(E)=0$ for $i<t$, [def-sbc-standard-tstructure-derived-category] represents $E$ by a bounded-below complex $L$. Choose its bounded-below injective K-injective resolution by [lem-sc-bounded-below-injective-resolution]. The bounded-below derived functor and our unbounded $R\Gamma$ are both represented by $F(I)$ for that same resolution. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-derived-functor-negative-vanishing] with $v=F$, $b=t$ and the Grothendieck categories established in step 2. It gives $H^mR\Gamma(X,E)=0$ for $m<t$. No upper bound is used, and this implication is independent of $C$, so the same $N$ serves both clauses.
